title: Route-level cost attribution + lightweight trace sampling: MVP scope reduction
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Summary: For the Console MVP we must reduce scope around cost dashboards and tracing to deliver value with minimal engineering effort. This ticket captures a targeted slice: provide route-level cost attribution (approximate, sampled) and a lightweight trace-sampling mechanism with deterministic sampling + error-triggered full capture. We explicitly cut features that increase surface area or storage needs for MVP: no per-API-key live-tail, no full-session traces retained >7 days, and no per-customer token-level billing export in MVP.

Background and motivation: Teams want actionable cost signals that map to application routes and model variants without waiting for the full observability surface. Full fidelity per-token billing and ubiquitous full traces are expensive and delay launch. A reduced scope that focuses on per-route attribution (approximate) + sampled traces delivers most product value for both platform and customers while keeping infra and storage costs predictable.

Scope (what we will deliver in MVP slice):
- Route-level cost attribution displayed in a new "Route Cost" dashboard card; costs are computed using sampled requests and model runtime metadata.
- Deterministic trace sampling at configurable rates (default 1%) with the option to set a higher sampling rate per-route in the Console.
- Automatic full-trace capture when a request triggers an error class (5xx or model-generation-failure) or when latency > SLA threshold; these full traces are stored for 7 days.
- Minimal schema for shown cost breakdown: route, model_variant_id, tokens_estimate, sample_weight. No proto-level token-by-token export.
- API to retrieve sampled trace IDs and aggregated route cost totals via Console query endpoints for dashboards.

Out-of-scope (explicit cuts):
- No per-API-key granular live tail or live streaming traces in MVP.
- No long-term trace retention beyond 7 days.
- No CSV export of per-token billing in MVP release.
- No advanced attribution using KV cache or batching heuristics for this slice (deferred).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Accuracy vs cost: Using sampling reduces storage and compute costs but introduces statistical variance in small routes; we mitigate with deterministic sampling and sample_weight correction in aggregates.
- Developer effort vs value: Avoiding per-token accounting and long retention reduces infra & compliance overhead and accelerates ship.
- User UX: Customers will see approximate costs for very low-volume routes; documentation and an in-UI confidence indicator will explain variance.

Acceptance Criteria (must be met for acceptance):
- Dashboard card "Route Cost" exists and shows route, model_variant_id, sampled_cost_usd, sample_count, sample_weight for the last 24h and last 7d.
- Costs are computed using sampling-corrected estimates; backend provides documented algorithm and evidence of unbiasedness for aggregate queries (link to brief included).
- Trace sampling obeys deterministic hash policy by request_id and respects per-route override from Console (default 1%).
- Error-triggered full-trace capture fires on defined error classes and is viewable in Console for up to 7 days.
- Performance: sampling introduces <2% p99 additional latency on the request path in our staging load tests.
- Storage: projected increase in storage for traces is within budget for MVP (<= +18% vs baseline) per capacity spreadsheet.
- Documentation: PRD, public Console tooltip copy, and engineering runbook published with links in this ticket.

Acceptance Test Plan (high level):
- End-to-end test that sends synthetic traffic across three routes: high-volume, low-volume, and error-heavy; verify sampled counts, weights, and corrected cost sums match expected with 95% CI.
- Simulate a model failure and confirm full-trace is captured and available in Console within 30s.
- Load test with sampling enabled to verify latency and storage projections.

Links and artifacts: [PRD] https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/route-cost-mvp-prd, [design mocks] https://drive.redwood.ai/console/route-cost-mocks, [capacity spreadsheet] https://sheets.redwood.ai/console-mvp-storage, [eng plan] https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/4821, [staging dashboard] https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/route-cost-mvp

Notes for engineering: The backend must expose a simple summary endpoint aggregated by route+model_variant that includes sample_count and sample_weight to correct totals. Use deterministic sampling based on sha256(request_id) mod 10000 < rate*10000 for consistency across services. Storage TTL for full traces set to 7d by default.
acceptance_criteria: Route Cost dashboard card renders route, model_variant_id, sampled_cost_usd, sample_count, sample_weight for 24h and 7d windows.
Sampling-corrected cost totals validated against synthetic traffic with documented methodology.
Deterministic sampling policy implemented and per-route override configurable via Console UI.
Error-triggered full-trace capture available in Console and retained for 7 days.
Performance and storage projections validated in staging (<2% p99 latency impact, storage within budget).
Docs: PRD, Console tooltip copy, and runbook published and linked from ticket.
